newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian metalworkers set fresh strike for Nov 15.
newsitem.headline: Italian metalworkers set fresh strike for Nov 15.

text.p: Italy's 1.5 million engineering and metalworkers will hold a fresh eight-hour strike on November 15 to press their pay claim, trades union officials said on Thursday.
They said the nationwide stoppage, which will follow a similar strike held on September 27, had been called by leaders of the FIOM, FIM and UILM unions at a joint meeting.

Negotiations between unions and employers over new contracts broke down last month. Unions have asked for a 262,000 lire pay rise per month to cover 1997-98, of which 97,000 lire would cover higher-than-expected inflation in the 1995-96 period.

The Italian metal industry employers' association, Federmeccanica, has rejected this demand, saying it would effectively increase the cost of labour by an average 20 percent for the three year period 1996-98.
Target inflation for the same three year period is just 8.4 percent. Employers have offered workers 180,000 lire.
A number of other sectors are awaiting the outcome of the dispute before completing their own round of pay negotiations. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
